pr_title: Fix sending wl "finished" events on monitor disabling. Fixes #1274
pr_body:
#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?
This PR should fix the issues in #1274, and in general should allow the usage of tools like `kanshi` or `shikane` for monitor management.  
Basically, now Hyprland does not send `finished` events when a monitor is disabled, allowing `kanshi`-like tools to hold references to the monitor resource.

#### Is there anything you want to mention? (unchecked code, possible bugs, found problems, breaking compatibility, etc.)
This is still in draft because more things should probably change. Notably:

- Disabled but not really removed monitors (like laptop built-in screens) are not deleted anymore from `realMonitors` and `monitors`. Does this cause any problem?
- I believe it would make more sense to avoid entering an unsafe state at all, if we have a disabled but still phisically attached monitor. For instance, we could simply re-enable the monitor (despite the user previously disabled it) and avoid unsafe states. This would also probably fix a lot of issues with unsafe state crashing on laptops.
- At the moment, unsafe states are still created, but without a headless monitor. This is because otherwise, in shikane/kanshi config, we would need to have profiles considering both the laptop screen and the headless monitor, which is undesirable imo.

#### Is it ready for merging, or does it need work?
As mentioned, it needs work. Also, I only tested with shikane but not with kanshi.

@vaxerski Sorry to tag you directly, but since this PR is changing core stuff, I would really appreciate your help :)
pr_comments: we're changing some stuff with this in #3713

Ok noticed. The main thing changing now is that the headless output is created at the beginning, so tools like `shikane` will probably see them. I'll check whether this causes "unexpected" behaviours when monitors are enabled with these tools (i.e., if you have 2 monitors, they'll see 3 and profile matching will fail).

That said, regarding monitor disabling, I think the best option would be to not go into unsafe state at all, and just enable whatever monitor is still in `realMonitors`. What do you think?

I confirm that with the new code tools like kanshi/shikane will not match any profile, unless one explicitly adds the headless output in their config files :/ Notice this is not related to monitor disabling only, but also to a "normal" situation where all monitors are connected and enabled.

1. no
2. disabled = not in m_vMonitors but in m_vRealMonitors
3. no. Sway does the same, what's your issue?

So, I tried to understand what Sway was doing different than Hyprland (considering the changes already done in this branch), and the thing mainly was that Hyprland was calling `wlr_output_layout_remove` on both monitor destroy and disable.  
Sway instead does not call this when the monitor is destroyed. The difference is that, if `wlr_output_layout_remove` is called, then the monitor is removed from `wlr_output_manager_v1` resources.  
The consequence is then that, when calling `wlr_output_manager_v1_set_configuration` after a monitor is destroyed, the [done](https://wayland.app/protocols/wlr-output-management-unstable-v1#zwlr_output_manager_v1:event:done) event is not sent for the removed monitor. This caused kanshi (but not shikane) to not update the profile.  
  
Sorry for the wall of text, but I think this might be helpful in the future. 
Coming back to your reply @vaxerski :  

1. fair enough, I removed that;
2. indeed, my bad;
3. sway does the same indeed. For me it was causing issues, but it was a "bug" on my branch. This is fixed now.

Given all this, the PR should be ready, I'll promote it to a real one. Please let me know if there's anything wrong here

issue_context.title: Disabling a monitor causes it to no longer be detected
issue_context.body:
Disabling through either kanshi, wlr-randr, or hyperctl makes the monitor undetectable through either.
So for example if I run `hyprctl keyword monitor LVDS-1, disable` , the monitor `LVDS-1` can no longer be found through: `hyprctl monitors`, or `wlr-randr`. Thus making it impossible to re-enable. Perhaps the issue that is being alluded to all the way at the end of #453. Perhaps this is even introduced by the fix?

running latest git version.
comments:
> So for example if I run hyprctl keyword monitor LVDS-1, disable , the monitor LVDS-1 can no longer be found through: hyprctl monitors, or wlr-randr.

Correct

> Thus making it impossible to re-enable.

Incorrect. Run `hyprctl keyword monitor LVDS-1,pref,auto,auto` and it will come back

And so it does. Reading the wiki I tried to create way to re-enable monitors regardsless of their name, through

`hyprctl keyword monitor ,pref,auto,auto`

but that doesn't work. Can I ask why it is removed, as opposed to disabled (like sway / wayfire do)?

It becomes more challenging to have kanshi automatically react to monitor disconnects, since it can't match anymore to the now removed internal monitor
disable does exactly what it says. I think you're confusing it with dpms.

That might very well be the case. The reason I bring it up, is that kanshi profiles disabling a display when an external monitor is connected, depend on the original still being found (though in disabled state) when external monitor is subsequently disconnected (as is apt to happen with laptop docking). This is how it does work with wayfire and sway. However due to hyperland actually removing (also through kanshi / wlr-randr) this plug and play behavior no longer functions.

the tooling can no longer differentiate between a disconnected and disabled monitor

I'll show some output of wlr-randr when disabling primary screen in another wlroots based comp.

```
LVDS-1 "LG Display 0x02EB (LVDS-1)"
  Physical size: 310x170 mm
  Enabled: no
  Modes:
    1366x768 px, 40.015999 Hz
    1366x768 px, 59.995998 Hz (preferred)
```

Note the `Enabled: no`
thats dpms

I am not saying it isn't,but the way to get that output still detected, but also in the disabled state is through kanshi, `wlr-randr --output bla disable `, etc.

consequence: no windows, or workspaces can be on that monitor.
Now with DPMS, there can be. It's late here now, but tomorrow I'll run a test that will show wlr-randr output in a DPMS powered down state. But the point is, the outcome of that won't imply that the disabled state can *only * be set through DPMS. (as we  know it can be done manually).

the fact is that hyprland removes monitors after wlr-randr disable, and sway/wayfire don't. It might also be that the others do it "wrong". However tools like kanshi expect their behavior, to enable this scenario:

1. laptop is docked
2. internal screen is "disabled", external screen enabled 
3. after undock, internal screen is re-enabled

step 3 will only work, if the internal monitor isn't removed after kanshi profile application (as happens with sway/wayfire and doesn't happen with Hyprland) .

of course manually re-enabling through `hyprctl keyword monitor LVDS-1,pref,auto,auto ` would work, but requires hardcoding internal display name.

So way too much words to say, could the different ways these compositors handle this be reason to consider not removing the monitor?
not really, no. You can always make a script to move all the workspaces out when you do dpms.
All but one, but yes. I can understand revisiting a design choice like this has impact.

For me neither. It's not a big deal, but as I mentioned in OP tooling expects the other behavior.

Running `hyprctl reload` re-connects all monitors for me. I have all of them defined in my `hyprland.conf` file.

I came across this fix by reading [this comment](https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/issues/2549#issuecomment-1603428605) on a similar issue.

Gosh, this is still happening, it would be nice if Hyprland had a way to define a fallback-monitor settings to try to re-enable it if there are no monitors marked as available.
The problem with using dpms instead of disabling is that the monitor will get the workspaces/windows anyway.

I've been investigating this a bit, but I have no time at the moment to fully understand how to implement something (will definitely try in the future), but I'll post my findings here, maybe they help somebody else (or vaxry himself, I'll tag him).

As mentioned, the problem is that apparently Hyprland is not exactly following the wayland protocol somewhere.

When a monitor is disabled, Hyprland is sending the `finished` and `done` signals via wl_roots (see my previous comment): this shouldn't happen. It seems to me that the reason this is happening is in `src/events/Monitors.cpp`, in the last line of function `listener_change`. That call to `wlr_output_manager_v1_set_configuration` is what is (then) activating the wrong signals. 
I'm not sure whether this function shouldn't be called at all in this case, or should be called but with a different `CONFIG` or `g_pCompositor->m_sWLROutputMgr` (aka `wlr_output_manager_v1`) state.

That said, I believe the problem is also in `src/helpers/Monitor.cpp`. I think the "actually completely destroy the monitor" signal is  sent by `wlr_output_manager_v1`, whereas the current connection to `wlr_output` should be used for the "disabling monitor" signal. I'm not too sure about this, in general my plan is to read sway code to understand what they're doing.

Once this is fixed, tools like kanshi or shikane can be correctly used in Hyprland too.
